facebook.content_angle: Early Vertical Forearm (high elbow catch) — how most club swimmers pull with a dropped elbow and lose propulsion on every single stroke, and the three-step drill fix that adds real distance per stroke before the next race
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers are pulling water with their forearm pointing at the pool floor. 🎯

That means every stroke is generating a fraction of the propulsion it should — and you are doing it hundreds of times per session without realising it.

The Early Vertical Forearm (EVF) fix changes everything:
👉 Bend your elbow to 90° at entry — forearm faces the wall behind you, not the bottom
👉 Drive your elbow HIGH before you pull — lead with the elbow, not the hand
👉 Feel your lats engage, not just your shoulder — that is where real freestyle power comes from

Once you feel it, you cannot unfeel it. ⚡

✔️ More distance per stroke with no extra effort
✔️ Less shoulder fatigue over long sets
✔️ The exact catch mechanics elite freestyle swimmers use at every distance

This autumn base phase is the best time to rebuild your catch from scratch — before race pace demands lock in bad habits.
